overview: The Medford Community Development Board reviewed proposed citywide zoning amendments for adult-use marijuana establishments and first-floor commercial requirements in multi-family districts. The board also conducted public hearings on the remanded Winthrop Estates subdivision and a proposed BJ's Wholesale Club fueling station, continuing both matters to August 2020.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The board voted to continue review and approval of the previous meeting's minutes to the August 2020 meeting.

items.title: Public Hearing: Adult-Use Marijuana Zoning Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: The board reviewed a proposed City Council zoning amendment regulating adult-use marijuana establishments and voted to recommend adding specific land-use table designations for allowed zones.

items.title: Public Hearing: Winthrop Estates Definitive Subdivision and Site Plan Review (541 & 551 Winthrop Street)
items.summary: The board reopened a public hearing on a remanded 10-lot subdivision application, reviewing updated ledge infiltration testing, water pressure data, and neighborhood impacts before voting to continue the hearing to August 20, 2020.

items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Amendment for First-Floor Non-Residential Uses in Multi-Family Districts
items.summary: The board voted to recommend adopting a mayoral petition requiring ground-floor commercial space in C1 and MUZ districts, while recommending that ground-floor commercial remain optional rather than mandatory in Apartment 1 and Apartment 2 districts pending comprehensive land-use planning.

items.title: Public Hearing: BJ's Wholesale Club Fueling Station Special Permit (278 Middlesex Avenue)
items.summary: Applicants presented revised site plans featuring new pedestrian walkways and complete-streets bicycle striping commitments along Middlesex Avenue, after which the board voted to continue the hearing to August 20, 2020.

items.title: Winthrop Place Subdivision Bond Reduction and Lot Release (25 Winthrop Place)
items.summary: The board voted to reduce the performance bond for the 25 Winthrop Place subdivision to $38,126 and recommended releasing the lots for full building permits.

items.title: Comprehensive Master Plan Request for Proposals (RFP) Discussion
items.summary: Staff and board members discussed the draft comprehensive plan RFP, agreeing to incorporate a 10-year action framework paired with a 30-year long-term vision prior to releasing the solicitation.
